name: Quantum
detail: The trained MPS contracts local feature tensors and squares amplitudes. Runs on a classical CPU; no quantum molecular dynamics or quantum hardware.
contract: Normalization and phase invariance tested. No calibrated quantum-to-molecule coupling.

name: Molecule
unit: HA size, OMV cargo classes, signaling links
detail: Inspect the sourced pathway atlas. HA molecular weight is metadata, not a learned efficacy coefficient. Single-vesicle cargo counts remain unknown.
contract: A scalar repair hypothesis enters the tissue model. No molecular reaction network is fitted.

name: Cell
detail: Cells are represented in the scene; barrier integrity and inflammation are aggregate indices. Individual cell signaling and communication are not simulated.
contract: Local-neighbor machinery is reusable, but fish alignment rules are not asserted to describe cell biology.

name: Tissue
unit: 20 tissue voxels; mass fractions; assumed time
detail: Conservative diffusion, directed transport, uptake and a hypothetical repair term. Neural predictions are checked against this solver.
contract: Distal tissue flux enters the blood compartment exactly once. Tissue-to-blood mass is conserved.

name: Organ
detail: A plaque capture/release compartment receives circulating tracer. The 3D outline is an illustrative extrusion of a published 2D figure.
contract: Blood-to-plaque flux is modeled. A whole heart, carotid tree or plaque-growth model is not implemented.

name: Organism
detail: The full organism is the story context. Systemic distribution to multiple organs, physiology and organism-level outcomes are not yet resolved.
contract: No tissue-clock extrapolation to whole-body transit or clinical outcomes.

name: Ecosystem
detail: Separation, alignment and cohesion generate collective motion. Compare individuals with coarse groups, disrupt local alignment, and measure recovery.
contract: Spatial bins, bounded neighbor sampling and count-preserving aggregation demonstrate scalability. This is not a calibrated aquatic ecosystem or food-web model.
